headline: Phillies take series finale from Nationals, 7-3
recap: Cristopher Sanchez struck out six over five innings to improve to 15-4, and the Phillies pounded out 16 hits in a 7-3 win over the Washington Nationals on Thursday night at Citizens Bank Park. Philadelphia scored in each of the first three innings for a 6-1 lead, then answered a pair of Washington runs with an insurance run of its own in the sixth. Bryson Stott went 2-for-3 with two doubles and an RBI, J.T. Realmuto had two hits, an RBI and two runs scored, and Brandon Marsh, Alec Bohm, Kyle Schwarber, Luis Arraez and Justin Crawford each added an RBI. Orion Kerkering was the only Phillies reliever to allow a run, in the sixth, before Jose Alvarado, Jonathan Bowlan and Jhoan Duran closed it out.

The win, part of a series in which Philadelphia took three of four from Washington, moved the Phillies to 62-54. They sit second in the NL East, 8.5 games behind the division-leading Atlanta Braves (70-45), and carry a one-game winning streak into their next series.

The Phillies open a three-game series at home against the Toronto Blue Jays on Friday, first pitch 6:40 PM ET at Citizens Bank Park. Zack Wheeler starts for Philadelphia against Toronto right-hander Jose Soriano. DraftKings has the Phillies as -210 moneyline favorites.
